questionsToConsider: How long is each type of appointment, and does the reason list reflect that?
What's the fastest you can really call back someone who needs to be seen today?
Do you need a date of birth or other ID to find a returning client's record?
What hours should the time picker offer, and do they change on some days?
guide.howToUseResponses: Check the urgent requests as they arrive and call back the ones who asked to be seen today first. For everyone else, use the reason to set the slot length: a first consultation needs longer than a routine check. Offer the preferred slot if it's free and the second choice if not. Pass the access needs to whoever greets the client, and send the reminder the way they asked.
customizeSteps: Rename the four reasons to your own appointment types, keeping the urgent one if you handle same-day requests.
Set the time window on both date questions to your opening hours.
Rewrite the urgent ending with the call-back time you can keep, then share the link on your website and booking pages.

faqs.q: What should an appointment booking form include?
faqs.a: Contact details, the reason for the appointment, a preferred date and time, a second choice and anything you need to arrange for the visit.

faqs.q: How do I handle urgent appointment requests?
faqs.a: Ask whether they need to be seen today and send those people to a separate ending that promises a call back, rather than a calendar.

faqs.q: Can the form ask different questions for new and returning clients?
faqs.a: Yes. First consultations and follow-ups each get their own questions here, and a routine check goes straight to picking a time.
No. It collects a request with a preferred time, which you confirm yourself, so you stay in control of your diary.
